title: De quibusdam eximiis proprietatibus circa divisores potestatum occurrentibus

deep.reconstruction:
Context: E557 studies which numbers are quadratic residues modulo a prime. Its earlier theorems show that if 4p-(2q+1)^2 is a prime P, then p is a quadratic residue mod P, since 4p ≡ (2q+1)^2 (mod P) and 4 is a square. Euler applies this along the families p = q^2+q±n.

(1) Scholion §14 (end): for a prime P = 4n+1, the tables on pp. 274-275 show that every prime factor of n-q^2-q (taken in absolute value) is a residue mod P. Euler stresses this is pure induction and still unproved. He warns that it holds only when 4n+1 is prime. His counterexample is n = 11 (modulus 45): the values n-q(q+1) are 11, 9, 5, 1, 9, 19, 31, 61, 79, 99. The factor 3 occurs, but 3 is not a square mod 45 (it is not a square mod 9). Euler guesses the success for primes comes from the large number of residues a prime modulus has.

(2) Conclusio §15: if 4n+1 is prime, all numbers n-q^2-q and all their prime factors are residues. In modern terms, take an odd prime r dividing q^2+q-n. Then (2q+1)^2 ≡ P (mod r), so (P/r) = 1, and quadratic reciprocity with P ≡ 1 (mod 4) gives (r/P) = 1. The factor 2 occurs only when n is even, i.e. P ≡ 1 (mod 8), where 2 is a residue by the second supplementary law. So the 'Conclusio' is equivalent to quadratic reciprocity for primes P ≡ 1 (mod 4); it is a conjecture, not a proof.

(3) Theorem 4 §16 and proof: if P = 4n-1 is prime, then every n+q^2+q is a residue. The proof sets p = n+q^2+q, so that 4p-(2q+1)^2 = P, and the earlier lemma applies. This is correct.

(4) Corollary 1 §17: reduced mod P, these values give at most 2n-1 classes. This is correct, since a prime 4n-1 has exactly (P-1)/2 = 2n-1 nonzero residues.

(5) Corollary 2 §18: hence all residues arise. This is true: n+q^2+q ≡ ((2q+1)/2)^2 (mod P), and q = 0, …, 2n-2 runs through all nonzero square classes. Euler adds the closure rules: if α and αβ are residues then β is; if αγ^2 is a residue then α is (for α, γ prime to P).

(6) Scholion §19 conjectures that every prime factor of n+q^2+q is also a residue mod 4n-1; it is tested on the following pages. In modern terms, an odd prime r dividing n+q^2+q gives (-P/r) = 1, and reciprocity for P ≡ 3 (mod 4) gives (r/P) = (-P/r) = 1. For r = 2, n must be even, so P ≡ 7 (mod 8), where 2 is a residue. Again the conjecture is equivalent to reciprocity, now for P ≡ 3 (mod 4).
errors: In the n=11 counterexample list Euler omits the value for q=7, namely 56-11=45=3^2·5. The list jumps from 31 to 61. This is harmless to the argument.

The explanatory remark 'pro divisore 2n+1 numerus residuorum semper est n' does not fit the setting, where the modulus is 4n+1 with 2n nonzero residues. It is either a slip or a loosely phrased heuristic. Either way the heuristic (counting residues) is not the real reason, which is reciprocity.

Corollary 2's justification ('quandoquidem etiam potestates quam producta ... inter residua reperiuntur') is not a valid reason why every residue appears. The conclusion is nevertheless true, by the bijection q -> (2q+1)/2 onto the nonzero square classes.
§15 is labelled a 'Conclusio' but rests only on induction, as Euler himself admits in §14.

ideas.what: Prime divisors of q^2+q-n (P=4n+1 prime) are quadratic residues mod P; failure for composite moduli illustrated with 45
ideas.modern_name: Quadratic reciprocity (case P≡1 mod 4) in Euler's 'divisor of quadratic form' formulation, with second supplementary law
ideas.where_published: E552 (Observationes circa divisionem quadratorum per numeros primos, Opuscula analytica 1783); E557 itself; earlier E164/E449 contexts; discussed by Weil and Lemmermeyer (Reciprocity Laws, ch. 1)

ideas.what: If 4n-1 is prime, every n+q^2+q is a residue, and these values give all 2n-1 nonzero residues
ideas.modern_name: Completing the square: n+q^2+q ≡ ((2q+1)/2)^2 mod P

ideas.what: Closure rules: α and αβ residues ⇒ β residue; αγ^2 residue ⇒ α residue
ideas.modern_name: Multiplicativity of the Legendre symbol / residues form a subgroup

ideas.what: Conjecture that all prime factors of n+q^2+q are residues mod the prime 4n-1

deep.surprise_reason: This is one of Euler's well-documented late inductive formulations of quadratic reciprocity, discussed by Weil, Lemmermeyer and others. The composite-modulus counterexample and the residue-counting heuristic are minor details, and nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'de numero 8 nihil plane concludere licet' — the digit is probably '3' (old typeface 3 resembling 8). The context, both the n=11 values 9 and 99 and the later 'circa numerum 3 nihil decidatur', concerns the prime 3.
